subject: Follow-up: prompt/output PII handling & retention — MedLytics
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Anna Liu <anna@medlytics.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Aug 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: prompt/output PII handling & retention — MedLytics

Anna — thanks again for the demo and the deep questions today. Quick written recap so we have alignment and clear next steps.

Call recap (high level):
- MedLytics uses our inference API to summarize patient notes and extract structured fields (PHI).
- Primary concerns: which parts of the request/response cycle are persisted, where data is stored (region), retention windows, access and audit logs, and guarantees around no-training / no-use for model updates.

What we heard you need from Redwood:
1) Explicit list of what Redwood persists by default for Hosted API customers (request metadata, prompt text, model outputs, KV cache, logs).
2) Options to make outputs ephemeral (no disk persistence) or short TTLs; confirm minimum configurable TTL and default TTL.
3) Data residency — need US-only hosting for this PoC and production.
4) Audit/logging retention (for incident response) and role-based access controls for logs.
5) Written commitment that customer prompt/output data will not be used for model training and how we enforce that.
6) A short matrix mapping common PHI fields to storage behaviors so your security team can sign off.

Attachments (attached):
- PII_Handling_Summary_MedLytics.pdf — our initial answers to the items above, and a proposed default configuration for the PoC.
- MAP_MedLytics.xlsx — suggested mutual action plan with milestones.

Please confirm whether the above captures everything. Specific asks from your side we need to close: a) the list of fields you consider PII/PHI (we can map them to storage behaviors), b) whether 30 days TTL is acceptable as a starting default or if you need 0/7/90, and c) availability for a security-focused technical call next week (30–45 min) to walk your SecOps.

Thanks —
Karthik Iyer
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachment: PII_Handling_Summary_MedLytics.pdf (summary + table)
Attachment: MAP_MedLytics.xlsx (mutual action plan)

From: Anna Liu <anna@medlytics.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: security@medlytics.com
Date: Sun, 29 Aug 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: prompt/output PII handling & retention — MedLytics

Thanks Karthik — this is helpful and close to what we discussed. A few clarifications from the security team: 

1) Retention: MedLytics requires audit/log data to be retained for 90 days for incident response. For prompt/output content (the actual text of prompts and generated outputs), we prefer the option to set TTL per-environment. For POC, we can accept 30 days, but production target is 0–7 days depending on environment.

2) Residency: US-only (AWS us-east-1) for the PoC and first 12 months of production.

3) Training/no-use: We need explicit language that customer prompt and output content are not used to train or improve Redwood models. This must be a contractual statement in the DPA or SOW.

4) PHI handling: We will send a canonical list of fields expected to be PHI (MRN, SSN, DOB, free-text notes that contain identifiers). Attached: MedLytics_PII_list.csv. Please map each field to your storage/retention outcome.

5) Auditability: We will need immutable audit logs that show read access to persisted prompt/output artifacts. Retention for audit logs: 365 days preferred.

Next steps: Can you update the PII_Handling_Summary with the items above and confirm the default and minimum TTL options? We are available for a technical call Tue/Wed next week (09:00–12:00 PT).

—Anna
Anna Liu
Head of Product Security — MedLytics
anna@medlytics.com
Attachment: MedLytics_PII_list.csv

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Anna Liu <anna@medlytics.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: prompt/output PII handling & retention — MedLytics

Anna — appreciate the detailed list. Below are our firm answers and configuration options for the PoC. I’ll also attach an updated one-page summary to the Drive link.

1) What Redwood persists by default (Hosted API):
   - Request metadata: timestamp, request-id, model/version, latency metrics — persisted in logs (retained per audit policy).
   - Prompt text (input): NOT persisted by default in an ephemeral-enabled configuration. For standard logging, prompt text is persisted only if customer enables request logging.
   - Model outputs: by default, Hosted API operates in "ephemeral outputs" mode for regulated customers — outputs are kept in memory for request processing and NOT written to disk. If a customer opts into persistence for debugging or analytics, outputs are written to encrypted storage with TTL.
   - KV cache / prefix cache: in-memory only for the runtime; not written to persistent logs unless debugging is explicitly enabled.

2) Retention TTLs and options:
   - Ephemeral mode: outputs are discarded immediately after response (0 days).
   - Short TTL mode: configurable to 1, 7, 30 days (customer choice).
   - Long TTL mode: up to 90 days for customers that require longer windows.
   - Default for PoC (per our suggestion): 30 days (can be lowered to 0 before production cutover).

3) Data residency / encryption / access controls:
   - PoC environment: AWS us-east-1 only (data-at-rest encrypted with customer or Redwood-managed KMS).
   - Role-based access controls: RBAC with audit trails; only named engineers (and support on opt-in basis) can request access.
   - Audit logs: request/response access logs are immutable and we can configure 365-day retention for logs related to the account.

4) No-use for training / contractual language:
   - Redwood will include a clause in the DPA and SOW: "Redwood will not use Customer prompt or output content to train or improve Redwood models, nor will it derive model training datasets from Customer data." We will circulate suggested DPA language before the legal review.

5) Mapping PHI fields to storage behavior:
   - We will map the MedLytics_PII_list.csv rows to three outcomes: Ephemeral (0), Short-TTL (1–30d), Persisted (30–90d). We will propose defaults but allow per-field overrides during the PoC.

6) Operational notes:
   - For debugging-only captures, customers can request time-limited logs; these must be approved by a named admin and are scrubbed for PHI unless explicitly permitted.

Next steps (concrete):
- I will upload an updated PII_Handling_Summary_MedLytics.pdf with the TTL matrix and proposed admin workflow by EOD today. (Drive link: https://drive.redwood.com/MedLytics/PII-Handling-Summary)
- Can we confirm Tue 2027-09-07 10:00 PT for the security tech call?
- Legal: I’ll ask Contracts to draft DPA language and circulate.

If this looks good I’ll mark the MAP milestone for the PoC config and schedule the technical call.

Thanks —
Karthik
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com
